newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND, UNITED SEEK TO REPEAT '60S SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND, UNITED SEEK TO REPEAT '60S SUCCESS.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund and Manchester United will both carry the hopes of a country as well as a city on their shoulders in the semifinals of the European Cup on Wednesday.
Germany and England boast two of Europe's most powerful leagues but have not won the world's most prestigious club trophy since Hamburg and Liverpool triumphed in 1983 and 1984 respectively.
Both teams will be seeking to repeat successes in the sixties when they begin Wednesday's first leg in Dortmund.

If the Germans reach next month's final in Munich they will have a chance to pick up their first European trophy since 1966 when they won the Cup Winners Cup. United are looking for a second European Cup triumph to go with 1968.
Many players involved on Wednesday were not even born when their clubs were making their names three decades ago, but they are well aware of the significance of the moment.
"When you are so close, you want to get into the final," Dortmund midfielder Andy Moeller said. "We can make history again. The whole of Europe, perhaps even the world, is looking at this game."
"Germany is one of the strongest nations together with Italy and Spain...Often our representatives were so close but did not get the right luck."

Although many of the players know each other from international football, this is a rare meeting of the clubs in Europe. The last time they clashed was in the 1964-65 UEFA Cup when the English team won 10-1 on aggregate.
Dortmund's preparations have been hit by injuries to Moeller and defender Juergen Kohler. But both will probably play.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld's biggest problem is how to replace suspended libero Matthias Sammer.
Brazilian defender Julio Cesar has no chance of making a comeback after a knee injury to boost the defence.

German international wing-back Stefan Reuter and Austrian Wolfgang Feiersinger are the two candidates for the position. But Reuter's attacking influence down the right flank is important to Dortmund and Feiersinger may be preferred.
Hitzfeld is likely to play the Austrian in a sweeper's role rather than a traditional attacking libero like Sammer, leaving Moeller as the main creative influence in midfield.

United need to tighten their defence after surprise 3-2 defeat by Derby at Old Trafford at the weekend. But manager Alex Ferguson believes his team are unlikely to make the same errors at the back again.
"Maybe their minds were already on this match here," Ferguson said after his team arrived in Germany on Monday. "But we will be ready for Wednesday."
But United are without injury worries entering the match and Ferguson has a full squad to choose from.
There will be more German police on duty in the Ruhr city than at any Dortmund match in the past since 500 English fans are expected to turn up without tickets.
But United's main problem in the Westfalenstadion may be getting used to a pitch which has looked bare in places in recent weeks, especially on the touchline near the main stand.
Expected teams:
Borussia Dortmund - Stefan Klos, Stefan Reuter, Juergen Kohler, Wolfgang Feiersinger, Joerg Heinrich, Lars Ricken, Paulo Sousa, Andy Moeller, Paul Lambert, Karlheinz Riedle, Stephane Chapuisat

Manchester United (from) - Peter Schmeichel, Denis Irwin, Gary Pallister, David May, Gary Neville, Phil Neville, Ronny Johnsen, Roy Keane, Nicky Butt, David Beckham, Ryan Giggs, Eric Cantona, Andy Cole, Ole-Gunnar Solksjaer.
